page.overview:
Who is Birdie?

Birdie's original design in 1987 was heavily based on Zeed, the first opponent faced by Kenshiro in the manga/anime series Fist of the North Star also known as Hokuto no Ken in Japan. He is named after the golfing term "Birdie." The other English character from the first Street Fighter game; Eagle, is also named after a golf term.

In the Alpha series, Birdie got his redesign as a hulking black man because the developers wanted the character to replace both muscle-bound characters from Street Fighter II which are both Zangief and Balrog. Birdie then became the first black British character in the series, followed by Dudley.

And in Street Fighter V, Birdie has been redesigned once again, but as an obese glutton because the developers wanted the character to replace both boyant characters from Super Street Fighter IV which are both Rufus and Hakan. Birdie gaining a significant amount of weight after retiring from professional wrestling is reminiscent to the many professional wrestlers who have let themselves go after their retirement. His current appearance is very similar to that of the late [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE WWE] wrestler [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viscera_(wrestler) Nelson Frazier Jr.], who was well-known by his wrestling ring names Mabel, Viscera, and Big Daddy V. Birdie's stomach tattoo has a similar design to that of current WWE professional wrestler, former [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultimate_Fighting_Championship UFC] fighter and former AEW professional wrestler [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CM_Punk CM Punk]. And his battle costume resembles the late [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_(band) Queen] frontman [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freddie_Mercury Freddie Mercury], as it has Freddie's jacket, mustache, and pants. Additionally, a crown is also placed upon Birdie's head.

Birdie's appearance has changed with each of the Street Fighter games that he is featured in, though he is generally depicted as a very tall (about the height of Sagat), late 1970s British punk rocker. In the original, he is shown as a tall, muscular man with pale skin a blonde mohawk (depicted as orange-red during combat); his outfit is that of a typical punk rocker with blue jeans, a dark leather vest, studded bracelets, and combat boots. Interestingly enough, Birdie's early Street Fighter V design was nearly identical to his original appearance.
